skill.name: firestore-security-rules-auditor
skill.description: Audit Firestore Security Rules for access control, validation, ownership checks, and update bypasses.
skill.summary: Reviews Firestore rules for common authorization and data validation failures.
skill.author: firebase

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 19 uses Markdown code spans around Firestore rule helper names. It does not invoke a shell or describe command execution.
Line 14 asks the auditor to compare create and update rules for bypasses. This is domain-specific rule review, not host or network reconnaissance.
Line 19 explains Firestore ownership checks for field updates. It does not instruct collection of system data or probing the host environment.

content.value_statement: Firestore rules often miss update bypasses, ownership checks, and validation gaps. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a focused security review.
actual_capabilities: Reviews create and update rules for state transition bypasses.
Checks whether sensitive authority fields come from trusted sources.
Assesses ownership checks around field-level update restrictions.
Flags missing type, length, and array size validation.
Scores findings from critical to secure using a five-point rubric.
limitations: Does not execute Firestore rules tests or emulator scenarios.
Depends on the provided rules and application context.
Does not replace a full security assessment.
May need project-specific data model details for precise severity.

use_cases.title: Review New Rules Before Release
use_cases.description: Find access control and validation issues before Firestore rules reach production.

use_cases.title: Triage Authorization Risk
use_cases.description: Identify likely privilege escalation, data exposure, and unsafe update paths in a rule set.

use_cases.title: Prepare Client Remediation
use_cases.description: Convert rule weaknesses into clear severity ratings and practical fix recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Rule Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small rules file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these Firestore Security Rules for obvious authorization and validation issues. Summarize the score, key risks, and fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Check Update Bypasses
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review of create and update differences.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the create and update rules. Identify any path where a user can create valid data, then update it into an unsafe state.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Ownership and Roles
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of identity and authority sources.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review how these rules verify owners, roles, and admin access. Flag any sensitive authority that depends on user-controlled document fields.

prompt_templates.title: Full Red-Team Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a rigorous Firestore rules audit using the app context below. Score the rules and report critical, major, moderate, and minor findings.

output_examples.input: Firestore rules for a user profile collection with create and update access.
output: Primary issue: update rules allow protected profile fields to change after creation.
Recommended fix: apply equivalent validation to create and update operations.

output_examples.input: Rules for a shared workspace app with members and owners.
output: Primary issue: membership data can grant access when it is written by the requester.
Recommended fix: base privileges on trusted membership records and strict ownership checks.

output_examples.input: Rules for a public content collection with authenticated writes.
output: Primary issue: text fields lack size limits and may allow storage abuse.
Recommended fix: add length limits and type checks for writable fields.

best_practices: Provide the rules file and the application data model together.
Ask for separate review of reads, creates, updates, and deletes.
Use local tests to verify high-risk recommendations.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a pass or fail without role and ownership assumptions.
Do not treat field whitelists as authorization checks.
Do not ignore create and update differences for sensitive fields.

faq.question: What does this skill audit?
faq.answer: It reviews Firestore Security Rules for authorization, validation, ownership, and update bypass problems.

faq.question: Does it execute tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and structured findings. Run your own tests to confirm behavior.

faq.question: Can it find privilege escalation?
faq.answer: Yes. It explicitly checks for self-assigned roles, unsafe admin rules, and user-controlled authority fields.

faq.question: What input should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the rules file, relevant data model, user roles, and expected read or write workflows.

faq.question: Is it only for new projects?
faq.answer: No. It can review new rules, existing production rules, or proposed changes before deployment.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
